1. Heard Shri Shree Ram, learned counsel for the applicants, Shri Pravesh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and Smt. Harshita Rani, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking quashing of the entire proceedings of Criminal case No. 1471 of 2025 (State Vs. Ashish Kumar and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 0593 of 2022 under section 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act police station Nawabganj District Prayagraj pending in the court of Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate -16 as well as the charge sheet No.
109 of 2023 dated 3.3.2023 and the cognizance/summoning order dated 15.7.2025.
3.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2 are husband and wife respectively.
There was matrimonial discord between them due to which the instant FIR has been lodged by the opposite party no. 2 against the applicants herein.
However, during the pendency of the said case parties have settled their dispute and a compromise has been executed between them on 25.7.2025, which was placed before the trial court.
Certified copy of the same has been annexed as Annexure-4 to the instant application.
Vide order dated 21.8.2025, this court had directed the parties to appear before the trial court concerned for verification of the compromise entered between them.

In terms of the order of this court the parties have appeared before the trial court on 30.8.2025 and in the presence of the parties the trial court has verified the compromise arrived at between them.
A report dated 3.9.2025 has been received from the C.J.M. Prayagraj to the effect that the compromise between the parties has been verified in the presence of the parties.
Thus learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case.

4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the aforesaid facts and admits the compromise entered into between the parties and its verification by the trial court.
5.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case learned for the State also does not oppose the prayer for quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case.

6. In view of the facts and circumstances, since it was a matrimonial dispute between the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.2, which has been amicably settled between the parties therefore no fruitful purpose will be served by keeping the criminal proceeding pending against the applicants herein and due to the aforesaid compromise, there are very remote and bleak chances of the conviction of the applicants.
Further, with the aforesaid settlement of matrimonial dispute, peace will prevail not only in the families of the parties but in society at large.

7. Thus, in the light of the judgments of the Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another : (2012) 10 SCC 303;
Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Ashish Kumar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129740431/
